title: Twice Upon a Time: Complementary Representations for Time-Series Reasoning
summary: Time Series Language Models (TSLMs) enable language-based understanding and reasoning over temporal data, yet a fundamental question remains: what information should their time-series representations preserve, and what variation should they factor out? Existing TSLMs typically expose the language model to a single representation, imposing a fixed inductive bias across downstream tasks. We instead introduce complementary representations as a design principle for time-series reasoning. Our model combines two visual views: line plots preserve absolute measurements and the observed coordinate frame, while normalized delay embeddings factor out positive amplitude rescaling and offsets while exposing temporal structure. Dedicated visual encoders integrate both views into a shared language model through visual tokens and multi-level feature fusion. Evaluation-time interventions verify that the two views exhibit distinct invariance profiles, while single-view ablations show that their combination is particularly beneficial beyond basic perception, with the large gains in prediction and reasoning. Built on Qwen3-VL-8B, our dual-view model improves overall TSRBench accuracy from 44.5% with line plots alone to 53.2%, substantially exceeding the strongest evaluated dedicated TSLM baseline at 36.7%. It further achieves 89.9% accuracy on TSExam and 86.8% numerical accuracy on multivariate ChatTS alignment. Together, these results demonstrate that complementary representations provide an effective design principle for general-purpose TSLMs, enabling models to exploit temporal structure without sacrificing access to the original measurement frame.
core_methodology: The paper introduces complementary representations for time-series reasoning by combining two visual views: line plots that preserve absolute measurements and normalized delay embeddings that factor out amplitude rescaling and offsets while exposing temporal structure. These representations are integrated into a shared language model through visual tokens and multi-level feature fusion.
data_sources: The methodology is evaluated on time-series data, likely including multivariate datasets as indicated by the mention of multivariate ChatTS alignment, though specific financial datasets aren't detailed.
alpha_potential: The dual-view approach could enhance predictive modeling in financial time series by capturing both absolute values and relative temporal patterns. This could improve momentum strategies, temporal pattern recognition, and anomaly detection in market data.
title_cn: 时间序列推理中的互补表示：双重视角
summary_cn: 该研究提出了一种双重视角的时间序列语言模型，结合保留绝对值的线图和展示时间结构的归一化延迟嵌入，显著提升了时间序列预测和推理能力。在量化交易中，这种方法可同时捕捉价格绝对水平和相对时序模式，对动量策略和市场异常检测具有潜在应用价值。

title: Where Backtests and Live Trading Part Ways: Six Defects from One Intraday System
summary: Backtests of intraday strategies can drift away from what the live system actually does; in our case, the drift never showed in summary statistics. We report six defects found while running one intraday US equity system live and comparing its live days with their backtest replay. Three came from data: a default feed that carried a small fraction of real opening volume, historical prices adjusted for dividends that live orders never see, and data the live system downloaded but the backtest never did. Two came from code: a sizing step that exceeded a limit the live account enforces, and UTC timestamps read as New York time. One came from configuration: settings that were switched on but never reached the code that places orders. For each we give the symptom, the size of the error, the cause and the test or control that now guards against it. All six sat where two paths that should agree had drifted apart. We close with a ten-point checklist. We make no claim about whether the system is profitable.
core_methodology: Comparative analysis between backtest results and live trading performance to identify discrepancies, specifically focusing on data, code, and configuration defects in intraday US equity trading.
data_sources: Intraday US equity market data, including real-time feed data and historical prices adjusted for dividends.
alpha_potential: Identifies systematic sources of divergence between backtest and live performance, which can lead to improved strategy robustness and reduced implementation risk in live trading environments.
title_cn: 回测与实盘分道扬镳之处：一个日内交易系统的六种缺陷
summary_cn: 该研究通过对比日内美国股票交易系统的回测与实盘表现，揭示了六种导致差异的缺陷类别（数据源差异、编码问题及配置错误），这些问题在传统统计指标中不可见。研究提出具体诊断方法和十项检查清单，对量化交易团队提升策略实盘可靠性具有重要实践价值。

title: How Much Screening Buys a Second? Speed, Selection, and the Maker's Spread
summary: We study the spread a liquidity provider needs to break even against counterparties that can exploit a stale quote, and we place two defenses on a single scale: repricing sooner and screening informed flow. A break-even condition pins down the exact screening rate at which a slower maker matches a faster unscreened venue: the selection that buys back the extra staleness. The result requires only an integrable price innovation and therefore holds under jumps, atoms, and infinite variance. Predictable drift is a centering problem: it widens a spot-centered quote, but its cost vanishes once the quote is recentered on the expected reference. In four USDC-WETH pools benchmarked against Binance ETH-USDT from June to August 2026, the one-second benchmark innovation is sharply non-Gaussian: 73% of seconds show no price change. Cutting cadence from twelve seconds to one sheds 84.5% of the expected shock, so a twelve-second maker must screen at least 84.5% of informed flow to match a one-second venue, far above the 71.1% that a Gaussian model implies. In trending markets, the stale pool is picked off at execution: with-trend fills obtain an effective spread 11.1 bps lower than against-trend fills, with the same sign in all four pools.
core_methodology: The paper analyzes the break-even spread for liquidity providers by considering two key defenses: frequent repricing and screening of informed flow. It establishes a break-even condition that links the screening rate to the staleness of quotes, providing a quantitative framework applicable under various market conditions including jumps and infinite variance.
data_sources: The study uses data from four USDC-WETH pools benchmarked against Binance ETH-USDT from June to August 2026, focusing on one-second benchmark innovations.
alpha_potential: The paper identifies a significant non-Gaussian behavior in price changes, where 73% of seconds show no price change. This insight can be leveraged to optimize liquidity provision strategies by adjusting quote cadence and screening rates, potentially yielding alpha by reducing adverse selection.
title_cn: 多少筛选能赢得一秒？速度、选择与做市商价差
summary_cn: 本研究通过分析流动性提供者在面对信息流时的两种防御机制（更频繁的定价调整和信息流筛选），为做市商价差提供定量分析框架。基于四个USDC-WETH池的数据，研究发现价格变动高度非高斯分布，73%的秒级无价格变化，优化报价频率可大幅降低预期冲击。这一发现对优化流动性策略、降低逆向选择风险具有实际应用价值。

title: PathFM: Fast Generative Forecasting of Multivariate Trajectories
summary: Time series foundation models are becoming increasingly popular for general-purpose forecasting. However, most leading models predict marginal quantiles, leaving the dependence structure of future trajectories unspecified. This distinction matters for trajectory-dependent quantities such as cumulative demand, peak load, and event timing, yet point and marginal scores do not reveal it. To model this dependence, we introduce PathFM, a trajectory-based forecasting model that uses flow matching to generate complete future paths. We further distill the model to one or two steps and share history attention cache across draws. Together, these enable PathFM to generate multiple paths for a single series in roughly the time needed for one query to a quantile model. The distilled sampler also makes it practical to optimize a calibration loss directly. PathFM achieves competitive marginal accuracy on the established forecasting benchmarks fev-bench and TIME. To complement these evaluations, we introduce Forecast Path Score Bench (fps-bench), which augments fev-bench tasks with energy and variogram scores and downstream metrics. PathFM achieves a higher aggregate path score on fps-bench than all evaluated external baselines. Experiments on chaotic systems further show that our flow model sustains long-run variability, while strong baselines rapidly collapse. PathFM makes generative time series forecasting both competitive and practical, enabling diverse downstream applications.
core_methodology: Flow matching-based generative forecasting model that generates complete future trajectories (paths) for multivariate time series. Key innovations include: 1) Distillation to one or two steps for efficiency, 2) Shared history attention cache across draws, enabling faster multi-path generation than quantile models.
data_sources: Generic multivariate time series data (demonstrated on fev-bench and TIME forecasting benchmarks), potentially applicable to market data including: asset price series, order book dynamics, macroeconomic indicators.
alpha_potential: Addresses critical limitation of marginal quantile models in finance by capturing dependence structure in trajectories - crucial for applications like: 1) Path-dependent options pricing, 2) Risk estimation of drawdowns/peaks, 3) Optimal execution where entire future path matters. The maintained long-run variability (vs. competitor collapse) suggests robustness for volatile market regimes.
title_cn: PathFM: 多变量轨迹的快速生成式预测
summary_cn: 该论文提出PathFM模型，通过流匹配技术生成完整未来路径，解决了传统分位数模型无法捕捉轨迹依赖性结构的痛点。对于量化交易，该技术可直接应用于路径依赖型衍生品定价、风险价值测算（尤其极端行情）及算法交易优化等场景，其保持长期波动性的特性相比现有方法更适合真实市场环境。

title: Causal Integrated Gradients: Scalable Feature Attribution Along Causal Paths
summary: Existing feature attribution methods that account for feature dependencies do not scale to high dimensions. We propose causal integrated gradients (CIG) and causal expected gradients (CEG), which extend integrated gradients to incorporate prior causal structure among input features while retaining its computational efficiency and, under conditions on the causal graph, its axiomatic guarantees. In many settings, some causal structure between features is already known, for example, that a transcription factor causally regulates a target gene's expression. Yet existing gradient-based methods cannot exploit this structure, instead crediting a feature's downstream effects over its true upstream cause, such as ranking the target gene above the transcription factor that regulates it. Our key idea is to embed this causal structure by routing the integration path along the causal graph. The method thereby decomposes each feature's attribution into a direct effect and effects mediated through its causal descendants. We evaluate CIG in three settings of increasing realism. First, on a synthetic benchmark with a known causal model, CIG's attributions best match the ground-truth causal effect from Pearl's do-calculus, matching the accuracy of causal Shapley values at a fraction of the computational cost. Second, on simulated single-cell gene expression data with a known gene regulatory network (Dyngen), CIG most accurately recovers the transcription factors driving the simulation. Third, on real interferon-$β$ stimulation data, where only an approximate causal graph is available, CIG better prioritizes the transcription factors driving the measured response than DeepSHAP and integrated gradients. Together, these results show that incorporating causal structure into gradient-based attributions recovers upstream drivers that existing methods miss, without sacrificing scalability.
core_methodology: Causal Integrated Gradients (CIG) extends integrated gradients by incorporating prior causal structure among input features, routing the integration path along the causal graph to decompose each feature's attribution into direct and mediated effects.
data_sources: Gene expression data (simulated and real), including single-cell gene expression data with known gene regulatory networks and real interferon-$β$ stimulation data.
alpha_potential: The method can be adapted to financial markets to identify upstream drivers of price movements or other market behaviors by leveraging known causal relationships, potentially uncovering hidden factors that traditional gradient-based methods miss.
title_cn: 因果积分梯度：沿因果路径的可扩展特征归因
summary_cn: 本文提出的因果积分梯度（CIG）方法通过整合已知的因果结构，改进了特征归因的准确性。在金融交易中，该方法可帮助识别价格波动的深层因果驱动因素，优于传统梯度方法，具有较高的实用潜力。

title: Momentum, Commentary Tone, and Earnings Surprise in LLM Financial Forecasts
summary: Which inputs drive a language model's financial forecast? We construct synthetic earnings announcements that independently reverse 20-day momentum, non-informational commentary tone, and whether fixed actual EPS beats a manipulated consensus. Six instruction/chat checkpoint conversions from four families (0.49-7.61B base parameters) receive 2,016 prompts each under a direct-answer Q8_0 protocol. The design includes 24 numerical blocks, six commentary pairs, profits and losses, rising and falling annual EPS, and two surprise sizes. Both A/B answer assignments and U/D cover all 384 primary scenarios per conversion. We estimate matched changes in conditional answer-prefix scores, not calibrated market probabilities. Across these checkpoints, the primary EPS contrast ranges from -0.19 to 86.80 percentage points. The magnitude of the primary signed tone contrast exceeds that of EPS in 5 of six models, and momentum exceeds it in 5. Natural-word numerical diagnostic accuracy ranges from 51.0 to 95.8 percent. Answer-encoding, wording, context, and conversion controls qualify these results. The experiment measures observable input reliance and numerical recognition; it establishes neither an internal reasoning mechanism nor realized return predictability. Public benchmark prompts, recorded scores, and an interactive recorded-results explorer accompany the study.
core_methodology: Experimental design using synthetic earnings announcements to test how LLMs respond to different financial inputs (momentum, commentary tone, earnings surprise) across multiple model checkpoints, measuring conditional answer-prefix scores rather than calibrated probabilities.
data_sources: Synthetic earnings announcements (controlled variations in numerical blocks, commentary pairs, EPS trends, and surprise sizes) with systematically manipulated inputs.
alpha_potential: Identifies which inputs (tone > EPS in 5/6 models, momentum > EPS in 5/6 models) LLMs overweight in forecasts - suggests potential misalignment between model focus and true signal sources. Findings could inform: 1) NLP-based trading factor construction 2) Detection of LLM bias in market-impacted contexts 3) Synthetic data approaches for financial fine-tuning.
title_cn: 大规模语言模型金融预测中的动量、评论语气与盈利意外
summary_cn: 通过构建合成盈利公告系统测试不同规模LLM对三大要素(20日动量反转/非信息性评论语气/盈利意外)的依赖度。实验发现模型普遍高估语气信号(5/6模型)和动量信号(5/6模型)而低估实际EPS信号，揭示算法交易中需警惕的LLM预测偏差模式。研究为设计抗干扰的NLP量化因子提供实证基础。

title: SelectPFN: Amortized Bayesian Variable Selection for Sparse Nonlinear Regression with Prior-Data Fitted Networks
summary: Tabular foundation models based on prior-data fitted networks (PFNs) predict on a new data set in a single forward pass, but they cannot report which inputs their predictions depend on. We propose SelectPFN, a PFN that performs Bayesian variable selection and prediction jointly for sparse nonlinear regression. In one forward pass it returns posterior inclusion probabilities for every variable, and its predictions are computed from sampled subsets only, so excluded variables provably cannot affect them; we show this is exactly what the Bayesian model prescribes. The network is pretrained once on synthetic tasks from a meta-prior built around a group spike-and-slab sparse-input neural network. Column-permutation equivariance combined with random interleaving of original and knockoff columns yields knockoff statistics with exact finite-sample false discovery rate control, even when the meta-prior is wrong. We develop theory for amortized selection: a Bayes-regret bound for the amortized median probability model, a characterization showing that the information needed to detect a variable grows like $(2/λ)\log(1/ω)$ in the prior weight $ω$ of structures that can use it, where $λ\le1$ is an efficiency, and a negative result showing that average-case training does not transfer to frequentist guarantees at a fixed truth. On out-of-prior nonlinear designs with p up to 500, SelectPFN improves the area under the precision-recall curve by 0.23-0.28 over the lasso, BART, DART, LassoNet and a group-penalized sparse neural network, at a false discovery proportion of about 0.07 and 0.04 seconds per data set. The advantage persists on real covariate matrices, and, as the theory predicts, detection of interaction-only variables rises monotonically with their prior weight.
core_methodology: The paper introduces SelectPFN, a prior-data fitted network that performs Bayesian variable selection and prediction jointly for sparse nonlinear regression. It uses synthetic tasks from a meta-prior to pretrain once and then, in a single forward pass, returns posterior inclusion probabilities for every variable and predictions computed from sampled subsets only. The approach includes strategies for exact finite-sample false discovery rate control.
data_sources: As the model is trained on synthetic tasks, the real-world application could involve financial datasets, such as time-series of asset prices or macroeconomic indicators.
alpha_potential: SelectPFN's ability to accurately select relevant variables for nonlinear regression could be valuable in identifying predictive signals in noisy financial data, thereby enhancing trading strategy performance. Its control over false discovery rates is particularly useful to avoid spurious correlations.
title_cn: SelectPFN：基于先验数据拟合网络的稀疏非线性回归贝叶斯变量选择方法
summary_cn: 本文提出一种贝叶斯变量选择方法SelectPFN，适用于稀疏非线性回归，能同时进行变量选择与预测。该方法在金融数据中可有效识别相关变量，提高信号识别效率并控制误发现率，适用于量化交易策略的变量筛选与预测模型优化。

title: Provably Efficient Risk-Sensitive Offline Reinforcement Learning via Optimized Certainty Equivalents
summary: Risk-sensitive reinforcement learning (RL) addresses decision-making under uncertainty and adverse outcomes. Learning risk-sensitive policies from fixed datasets is important when additional interaction with the environment is costly. Existing work on risk-sensitive RL focuses on online settings or specific risk measures, leaving a general theoretical understanding of its offline setting underdeveloped. In this work, we investigate efficient offline risk-sensitive RL using the optimized certainty equivalent (OCE), a general class of risk measures. We consider two formulations: dynamic-OCE RL, which applies OCE recursively at each step, and static-OCE RL, which applies a single OCE to the cumulative rewards. Under the tabular setting, we develop pessimistic value-iteration algorithms for both formulations and establish tight sublinear suboptimality bounds, explicitly capturing how risk sensitivity, encoded by utility functions, affects learning difficulty. Moreover, we establish minimax suboptimality lower bounds to characterize the problem's fundamental limits. To handle large state spaces, we further develop pessimistic least-squares value-iteration algorithms that incorporate the general OCE risk criterion into linear function approximation. We establish utility-dependent sublinear guarantees with explicit dependence on the feature dimension $d$. To our knowledge, we provide the first offline algorithms along with the first upper and lower suboptimality bounds for both dynamic- and static-OCE RL.
core_methodology: The paper develops pessimistic value-iteration algorithms for offline risk-sensitive reinforcement learning using optimized certainty equivalents (OCE). It considers both dynamic (recursive) and static (cumulative reward) applications of OCE and provides theoretical guarantees under tabular and linear function approximation settings.
data_sources: Fixed datasets (offline setting) for risk-sensitive decision-making, which could be adapted to historical market data in financial applications.
alpha_potential: The method could be adapted to optimize trading strategies under risk constraints by learning from historical data without additional environment interaction, potentially improving risk-adjusted returns.
title_cn: 基于优化确定性等价的可证明高效风险敏感离线强化学习
summary_cn: 该论文开发了离线风险敏感强化学习算法,适用于需要从固定数据集学习且避免实际交互的场景。其优化确定性等价(OCE)方法可被金融领域用于开发风险敏感的交易策略,直接从历史市场数据中学习最优决策。

title: Q($γ_H$): Entropy-Guided Horizon Mixing in Multi-Discount Q-Learning
summary: A fixed discount factor in Q-learning imposes a single planning horizon throughout training, despite the differing demands of early exploration and long-term credit assignment. We propose Q($γ_H$), a multi-horizon Q-learning framework that maintains multiple discount-specific heads and adaptively combines them at control time using an entropy-derived confidence signal. The resulting state-dependent mixing weights shift control from shorter- to longer-horizon heads as policy confidence increases, enabling adaptive horizon mixing without modifying individual Bellman updates. Across classical control and deep reinforcement-learning benchmarks, Q($γ_H$) shows its strongest improvements on delayed-credit tasks relative to strong fixed-discount baselines. By decoupling horizon adaptation from the underlying learning updates, Q($γ_H$) provides a lightweight framework for adaptive planning-horizon control in reinforcement learning, avoiding the need for manual discount-factor selection while remaining compatible with standard value-learning methods.
core_methodology: Q($γ_H$) introduces a multi-horizon Q-learning framework that maintains multiple discount-specific heads and adaptively combines them using an entropy-derived confidence signal. This allows for state-dependent mixing weights that shift control from shorter to longer horizons as policy confidence increases.
data_sources: Not explicitly mentioned in the abstract, but typically involves reinforcement learning environments and potentially financial time-series data in applied contexts.
alpha_potential: The adaptive planning-horizon control can be particularly useful in trading strategies that require balancing between short-term exploitation and long-term strategic positioning, such as portfolio optimization or execution algorithms.
title_cn: Q($γ_H$)：多折扣Q学习中的熵引导混合规划周期
summary_cn: Q($γ_H$)通过维护多个特定折扣的头并使用熵导出的置信信号动态组合它们，实现了状态依赖的混合权重，使得策略从短期到长期的平滑过渡。这种方法在量化交易中特别适用于需要平衡短期机会与长期战略的投资策略。

title: In-Context Preference-Conditioned Pareto Set Learning from Limited Offline Data
summary: Multi-objective optimization involves diverse preferences over conflicting objectives. Rather than returning a finite set of trade-off solutions, preference-conditioned Pareto set learning seeks to map a specified preference directly to a corresponding Pareto optimal solution. Yet in many real-world scenarios, optimization must proceed offline without further objective evaluations, leaving only a limited static dataset that sparsely covers the decision and objective spaces. Existing methods either optimize separately for each preference or train a problem-specific Pareto solution model, requiring repeated search across preferences or repeated training across problems. We introduce in-context preference-conditioned Pareto set learning (ICPSL), a framework that amortizes both preference-wise solution search and problem-specific model construction. ICPSL pretrains a foundation-style hypernetwork on a large and diverse set of synthetic prior data. Given the offline observations of an unseen problem, the pretrained hypernetwork learns to generate a problem-specific, preference-conditioned Pareto solution model in a single forward pass. The generated model can then be reused to predict solutions for arbitrary preferences without problem-specific training or preference-wise search. Experiments on synthetic and real-world problems show that ICPSL produces high-quality Pareto solutions while providing substantial speedups in problem-specific solution-model construction.
core_methodology: In-context learning framework for preference-conditioned Pareto set learning, using a pretrained hypernetwork to generate problem-specific Pareto solution models efficiently
data_sources: Synthetic prior data for pretraining, then limited offline observations from real-world problems
alpha_potential: Enables rapid generation of optimal portfolios under varying risk/reward preferences in offline settings, potentially improving multi-objective portfolio construction
title_cn: 基于有限离线数据的上下文偏好条件帕累托集合学习
summary_cn: 该研究提出一种新型多目标优化框架，通过预训练超网络在未见问题上快速生成符合特定风险偏好的帕累托最优投资组合。相比现有方法需反复优化的不足，该技术仅需单次前向传播即可完成组合构建，为量化投资中的离线组合优化决策提供高效解决方案。

title: When Does "Post-Call" Begin? An Availability Contract for Earnings-Call NLP Benchmarks
summary: Corporate financial disclosures often unfold over time, with announcements, prepared remarks, and discussion spanning multiple high-frequency return intervals. Financial NLP benchmarks can therefore suffer from a within-event timing mismatch when the prediction target begins before the textual or audio input used by a model could be complete. Chronological train--test splits do not prevent this mismatch, because it occurs inside individual events rather than across samples. We introduce an Availability Contract, which requires a benchmark to state the input boundary, evidence for input availability, the outcome start, and the claims supported by that evidence. We apply this framework to 552 earnings calls from 24 firms. For each call, we hold the return endpoint fixed and compare the previous close, a documentary call-start proxy, and a completion proxy based on reconstructed audio end plus a stipulated processing allowance. At this baseline, moving from the call-start proxy to the completion proxy flips return signs for 9.4% of calls. Holding completion-clock cutpoints fixed, 28.3% change quintile. In an independent release-session analysis of a public earnings-call volatility benchmark, shifting before-market target windows forward by one trading session raises three-day mean squared error by 18.1-21.4% across four frozen prediction streams, while their point rankings remain unchanged. Together, the results show that labels and losses can depend materially on the declared outcome clock even when model rankings appear stable. The Availability Contract makes this assumption explicit and ties post-input claims to the available timing evidence.
core_methodology: The paper introduces an Availability Contract framework to address timing mismatches in financial NLP benchmarks, specifically focusing on earnings calls. It provides a structured approach to define input boundaries, evidence for input availability, outcome start times, and the claims supported by that evidence. The methodology involves comparing different proxies for call-start and completion times to assess their impact on return signs and quintile changes.
data_sources: The study uses 552 earnings calls from 24 firms, along with high-frequency return intervals and reconstructed audio data for timing analysis. It also references a public earnings-call volatility benchmark for independent validation.
alpha_potential: The research highlights the material impact of timing assumptions on labels and losses in earnings-call analysis. By explicitly defining input and outcome timing, it can help improve the accuracy of NLP models used in trading strategies that rely on earnings call transcripts. This could lead to better detection of market reactions and potential alpha generation from timely and precise interpretation of earnings call content.
title_cn: “盘后电话会议”何时开始？为财报电话会议NLP基准制定的可用性合同
summary_cn: 本研究通过引入可用性合同框架，解决了财报电话会议NLP基准中的时序错配问题，明确了输入边界和结果时间。实证分析显示时序假设对标签和损失有显著影响，可提升交易策略中NLP模型的准确性。适用于依赖财报电话内容的量化交易场景，提升市场反应捕捉能力。

title: NEST: Stale-Robust Tokenized-Stock Measurement for a Crypto-Treasury LETF Stack
summary: Tokenized equities trade while listed markets are closed, so their marks could improve off-hours measurement along layered exposures that link Bitcoin, crypto-treasury stocks, and leveraged ETFs. A token return and the next opening gap, however, share the price move from the previous close to the token mark, so part of their apparent fit is mechanical. We develop NEST, a stale-robust protocol that separates this shared-history fit from conditional measurement value. A shared-history identity and a variance-clock bound show how much fit timing alone can generate. The partial determination index (PDI), the squared partial correlation between token and gap given public controls, measures what remains, and a finite-sample frontier expresses the partial-F decision in PDI units. Product, provenance, timestamp, and execution audits decide whether an informative mark is admissible. For MSTRx, a tracker certificate on MicroStrategy (MSTR), a token-only $R^2$ of 0.916 shrinks to a modest increment once Bitcoin, mark age, and a pre-09:00 MSTR premarket proxy are controlled: the token explains 15.7% of the remaining gap variation (1% frontier 0.031), and 14.0% to 17.0% under stricter clock variants, including one in which every token mark precedes 09:00. A trade-level reconstruction on Gate gives 25.2%; NVDAX and AAPLX clear their frontiers, whereas TSLAX does not. An admitted mark updates, rather than replaces, BTC-unit exposure diagnostics for the BTC-MSTR-LETF chain.
core_methodology: NEST protocol for stale-robust measurement that separates shared-history fit from conditional measurement value using partial determination index (PDI) and variance-clock bound to evaluate tokenized equity data quality and information content.
data_sources: Tokenized equities (MSTRx, NVDAX, AAPLX, TSLAX), Bitcoin, mark age, pre-market proxies, timestamp and execution audits from Gate.io and similar platforms.
alpha_potential: Identifies conditional information in tokenized stock prices after controlling for shared history with public markets. Shows 15-25% explanatory power for opening gaps, suggesting potential for off-hours signal extraction in BTC-linked equities and LETFs. Protocol enables filtered signal extraction from crypto-treasury asset chains.
title_cn: NEST：加密国库LETF堆栈中抗陈旧的代币化股票衡量协议

title: Learning to Forecast on Multiple Spatiotemporal Hierarchies
summary: Hierarchical forecasting exploits aggregation structures that expose multiple views of the same underlying spatiotemporal forecasting problem, while ensuring coherence among forecasts. Individual series provide fine-grained information, while progressively coarser aggregates reveal temporal and spatial patterns at different scales. In the associated deep learning architectures, the hierarchy determines which aggregate series are available and how they are processed together with individual series (e.g., through reconciliation or message-passing operators). Different hierarchies thus provide distinct learning signals and inductive biases for forecasting the same collection of time series. Nonetheless, existing architectures are typically trained on a single, often fixed, structure. In this work, we propose a graph deep learning framework that leverages variations across hierarchies as multi-task regularization. We show that jointly learning across these structures can reduce over-specialization to any single hierarchy and improve forecasting performance. Indeed, training across hierarchies provides an inductive bias toward representations that are useful across different structures, and as such, generalize better. Making forecasts coherent with the aggregation constraints for each sampled hierarchy is computationally expensive: to complement the framework, we propose a novel operator-based on a top-down approach-that produces coherent forecasts with linear time and space complexity w.r.t. the hierarchy size. Experiments show that our approach improves forecasting accuracy over training on a single structure and is competitive with current state-of-the-art methods.
core_methodology: Graph deep learning framework for hierarchical forecasting, leveraging multiple spatiotemporal aggregation structures as multi-task regularization. Introduces a top-down operator for efficient forecast coherence across hierarchies.
data_sources: Presumably time-series data with hierarchical aggregation structures (e.g., financial markets data with sector/asset class groupings, geographic hierarchies, or multi-frequency aggregations)
alpha_potential: Could extract signals from complex market microstructure interactions, improve volatility forecasts by leveraging multi-scale patterns, or enhance portfolio construction by maintaining coherence across asset hierarchies

title: Online Quantile Omniprediction for Proper Losses
summary: The task of constructing a predictor that is simultaneously accurate under multiple evaluation metrics has been popularized recently under the name omniprediction. Prior work in this area has largely focused on binary prediction tasks, and existing results for multiclass and continuous outcomes typically suffer from slow error rates. In this paper, we consider forecasts expressed as a set of quantiles over a discrete but otherwise arbitrary set of probability levels. We develop sample-efficient algorithms for constructing forecasts that are accurate simultaneously across all proper losses that satisfy mild regularity conditions, where proper losses are those minimized by predicting the true quantiles. Our algorithms are online and can operate in a dynamic environment, while simultaneously taking multiple losses into account, and their forecasts offer the potential to provide diverse end-users with rich information for evaluating risk and informing a range of practical decision-making tasks. As an example, we demonstrate how our procedure can be used to ensemble quantile forecasts of COVID-19 hospitalizations made by experts during the pandemic.
core_methodology: Development of online algorithms for constructing quantile forecasts that are accurate across multiple proper loss functions. The methodology focuses on discrete but arbitrary probability levels and ensures sample efficiency in dynamic environments.
data_sources: No specific market data mentioned in the abstract, but the methodology is applicable to any time-series data, such as financial returns, volatility, or economic indicators. Demonstrated application includes COVID-19 hospitalization forecasts, suggesting adaptability to various time-series datasets.
alpha_potential: The ability to generate accurate quantile forecasts across multiple loss functions can be valuable for risk management, volatility forecasting, and tail-risk hedging strategies in quantitative trading. The online nature of the algorithm makes it suitable for real-time trading environments.
title_cn: 在线分位数全预测在适当损失函数下的应用

title: DST-Net: Decomposed Spatio-Temporal Network for Time Series Forecasting
summary: Series decomposition has emerged as a widely acknowledged paradigm in deep time series forecasting models. However, existing approaches predominantly employ a homogeneous modeling strategy for all subsequences, thereby overlooking the distinct inductive biases inherent in different components. We identify that the trend component exhibits dominant spatial coupling across channels but carries significant temporal redundancy, whereas the seasonal component is characterized by local temporal evolution but remains susceptible to attention distraction. To address this, we propose a novel disentangled architecture that tailors specific modeling strategies to align with the intrinsic properties of each component. For the trend branch, we design a Latent Graph Block, employing latent graph modeling to capture global topological dependencies and system-wide co-movements. Conversely, for the seasonal branch, we introduce a Gaussian Multi-scale Attention mechanism to mitigate attention distraction. By injecting learnable Gaussian priors, we impose structural constraints that compel the model to focus on multi-granular local contexts, effectively filtering out global noise and accurately capturing local evolutionary phases. Extensive experiments on multiple real-world benchmarks demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed model.
core_methodology: The paper proposes a novel disentangled architecture for time series forecasting, decomposing series into trend and seasonal components. It employs a Latent Graph Block for global trend dependencies and Gaussian Multi-scale Attention for local seasonal patterns, addressing the distinct properties of each component.
data_sources: Multiple real-world benchmarks (specific datasets not mentioned in abstract but likely include standard time series datasets and possibly financial time series given the methodology's general applicability)
alpha_potential: The model's ability to separately capture global co-movements (trend) and local evolutionary patterns (seasonal) could identify persistent market anomalies or regime shifts, particularly in: 1) Momentum strategies by improving trend identification, 2) Pairs trading through enhanced co-movement detection, 3) Volatility forecasting via better seasonal pattern recognition
title_cn: DST-Net：分解时空网络用于时间序列预测

title: StochLOB: Heavy-Tailed Score Matching for Robust Limit Order Book Trend Prediction
summary: Score-based diffusion methods usually perturb data with Brownian Gaussian noise, corresponding to a light-tailed forward stochastic differential equation (SDE). For market time series this SDE can be a poor abstraction: limit order book (LOB) order flow is heavy-tailed, bursty, and occasionally jump-like. We study STOCHLOB, a training-only score-matching framework that changes the forward diffusion corruption law while leaving the deployed predictor deterministic. Instead of Brownian-only Gaussian corruption, the noising process uses two non-Gaussian SDE-inspired alternatives: jump-Lévy noise through a compound-Poisson variance mixture, and clipped $α$-stable noise through a positive-stable Gaussian scale mixture. These corruptions inject finite jumps and heavy-tailed residuals into training without requiring reverse-time diffusion sampling at inference. The resulting score target has a useful interpretation: its radial factor $h_t(r)$ is the posterior expected corruption precision, so large residuals are weighted according to the latent corruption scale that most plausibly generated them. On chronologically held-out Coinbase LOB data, the proposed variants remain competitive on uncorrupted BTC and altcoin test horizons and improve several realized tail-window stress diagnostics. An exploratory Feishu A-share transfer study further tests whether the probability outputs remain usable under transaction costs and trading-rule constraints. Code and configuration files are available at https://github.com/ArshiAbolghasemi/Penny.
core_methodology: Score-based diffusion framework that incorporates heavy-tailed noise (jump-Lévy and clipped α-stable noise) during training to better model limit order book dynamics, while maintaining deterministic prediction at inference time. The method focuses on robust trend prediction by adapting to the heavy-tailed nature of market data.
data_sources: Coinbase limit order book (LOB) data for Bitcoin (BTC) and altcoins, with exploratory testing on Feishu A-share data under trading constraints.
alpha_potential: The method captures heavy-tailed and jump-like behavior in order flow, potentially improving trend prediction during volatile market conditions. The explicit modeling of tail risks may provide better signal quality for momentum-based strategies or market-making algorithms.

title: LEV: Thinking Fast and Deep with Looped Decision Models
summary: Decision models answer typed questions about an input with one probability per option, computed in a single forward pass without generating text. Like the fast System 1 of dual-process theory, they answer at once, but their depth is fixed at training time, so they spend the same computation on easy and hard questions. Models that reason in generated text can think longer, but they pay for every extra step in decoded tokens. We present LEV, a decision model that thinks deeper by rerunning its layers in a loop instead of generating tokens. LEV builds on a language model pretrained as a loop, reads the options after every loop step and trains all steps jointly, so one checkpoint can answer at any depth. On three looped backbones, accuracy rises with depth on the same weights, mostly on hard questions, and a 2.6B LEV goes from 63.2% at depth one to 76.2% at depth four on JevBench. On-demand depth, set per question by a small stopper with a threshold fitted on unlabelled requests, saves 15% to 24% of the computation at a cost of under one accuracy point, level with or slightly above a fixed mix of depths. On a locked test set, the 1.4B and 3B models are 5.4 to 8.8 points more accurate than dense (non-looped) models and cascades of the same latency below 50 ms.
core_methodology: LEV introduces a decision model that dynamically adjusts its computational depth by looping through model layers and reading options after each loop step, enabling on-demand depth adaptation for different question difficulties without generating text.
data_sources: The paper does not specify financial datasets but demonstrates performance on JevBench, suggesting potential applicability to market prediction or decision tasks.
alpha_potential: The model's ability to adapt computational depth on-the-fly offers potential for efficient real-time decision-making in trading scenarios, particularly for latency-sensitive tasks where computational resources must be optimized without sacrificing accuracy.
title_cn: LEV：通过循环决策模型实现快速深度思考

title: Stochastic Gradient Descent: A Nonlinear Time Series Perspective
summary: This paper investigates the statistical behavior of Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD) with constant step size under the framework of iterated random functions. Compared to previous studies establishing the convergence of SGD in probability measure, e.g., Wasserstein distance, our approach directly provides the convergence in Euclidean distance by showing the Geometric Moment Contraction (GMC) of SGD. This new convergence can address the non-stationarity of SGD due to fixed initial points and can provide a more refined asymptotic analysis of SGD. Specifically, we prove quenched central limit theorem, invariance principle and $α$-stable convergence for averaged SGD (ASGD) regardless of initialization. Furthermore, we provide a novel perspective to understand the impact of step sizes in SGD by studying its derivative with respect to the step size. The existence of stationary solutions for the derivative processes is shown, enabling the use of interpolation to recover the full-trajectory of SGD. Subsequently, we utilize multiple step sizes and show an enhanced Richardson-Romberg extrapolation with improved bias representation, which brings ASGD estimates closer to the global optimum. Finally, we propose a new online inference method and a bias-reduced variant for the extrapolated ASGD. Empirical confidence intervals are constructed and the coverage probabilities approach the nominal level as $n$ grows.
core_methodology: The paper advances the understanding of Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD) in a nonlinear time series context, particularly focusing on the convergence properties in Euclidean distance rather than probability measure. It introduces a novel perspective on the impact of step sizes in SGD and proposes an enhanced Richardson-Romberg extrapolation method to improve the bias representation of averaged SGD (ASGD) estimates. Additionally, it offers a new online inference method and a bias-reduced variant for extrapolated ASGD.
data_sources: While the paper does not specify financial market data sources, the methodologies are theoretically applicable to financial time series data, such as stock prices, returns, or other market indicators.
alpha_potential: The research has significant potential for quantitative trading by improving the optimization of trading strategies. The enhanced convergence properties and bias-reduced SGD variants could lead to more stable and accurate predictions in financial models, potentially uncovering inefficiencies in market data through improved machine learning model training.

title: Learning Self-Orchestration in Decentralized Agent Swarms
summary: The capabilities of an agent swarm depend on both its individual members and how they coordinate. Yet existing multi-agent systems often train agents within fixed orchestration structures, separating the learning of individual capabilities from the organization of collective behavior. We introduce market-based post-training (MPT), a framework for jointly learning action policies and self-orchestration in decentralized agent swarms. Agents express their willingness to participate through bids, which determine who acts and how collective outcomes provide local training credit. Learning both action and bidding behavior allows individual capabilities and patterns of participation to adapt together without a central coordinating agent. We evaluate MPT on embodied crafting, robot navigation, and deep research. Results show gains over monolithic post-training and confirm that agent participation indeed evolves with learning. With the same post-trained action policies, learned self-orchestration outperforms alternative coordination strategies. Ablations show that both action and bidding benefit from learning, and that learned bids provide more effective action-training signals. Beyond the original training objectives, trained swarms adapt faster to related tasks and achieve better performance with larger populations at inference time. Larger populations also suffer smaller performance losses under agent dropout, demonstrating that learned self-orchestration supports reuse, scaling, and robustness in decentralized agent swarms. Code and trained models are available at https://github.com/Embodied-Minds-Lab/MPT.
core_methodology: Market-based post-training (MPT) framework for learning self-orchestration and action policies in decentralized agent swarms using bidding mechanisms to determine participation and credit assignment
data_sources: Simulated environments (embodied crafting, robot navigation, deep research tasks)
alpha_potential: Potential applications in portfolio management as a decentralized coordination mechanism for multi-strategy systems or algorithmic execution. The adaptive coordination aspect could help with dynamic strategy allocation
title_cn: 去中心化智能体群中的自主学习协同机制

title: Decentralized LLM Workflows via Sequential Auctions
summary: We present a scalable framework for solving multi-step tasks through a decentralized market of self-interested agents. Prior theoretical work demonstrated that agents organized through sequential auctions can converge to a globally optimal policy in a Markov decision process (MDP), but relied on the restrictive assumption of the existence of perfect clones as a model of perfect competition. In reality, exact clones drive agent profit to zero, violating the natural risk-reward incentives of participants. Conversely, we empirically demonstrate that the opposite extreme, absence of competition, also leads to market failure and value extraction collapse. Between these two extremes, we investigate how heterogeneous agents can survive in markets that span the critical middle ground of imperfect competition. To be profitable, agents learn to strategically shade bids to secure positive individual profit margins, while still ensuring that the marketplace functions effectively enough so that collaborative tasks posed by market consumers can still be solved. We formulate and evaluate four bidding algorithms (Mirror Descent, Thompson Sampling, Bayes-Optimal, and PPO) across three auction protocols (1st-Price, 2nd-Price, and Credit-Conserving Vickrey). Across a diverse set of domains, we demonstrate that imperfect competition successfully sustains necessary agent profit margins while maintaining high task success rates at low costs.
core_methodology: The paper investigates decentralized markets of self-interested agents using sequential auctions, with four bidding algorithms (Mirror Descent, Thompson Sampling, Bayes-Optimal, and PPO) across three auction protocols (1st-Price, 2nd-Price, and Credit-Conserving Vickrey). The focus is on strategic bidding in imperfect competition to maintain profitability and task success.
data_sources: The paper does not specify financial market data but uses simulation domains to evaluate bidding algorithms and auction protocols.
alpha_potential: Potential applications include algorithmic trading strategies where agents (e.g., trading algorithms) compete in decentralized markets, optimizing bids to secure profitable trades while maintaining market efficiency. This could be adapted to high-frequency trading or dark pool liquidity provision.
title_cn: 通过序贯拍卖实现去中心化大型语言模型工作流程
summary_cn: 本文研究通过序贯拍卖实现自利代理在去中心化市场中的多步骤任务协作，探索战略竞价在非完全竞争市场中的盈利特性。四种竞价算法在三种拍卖协议下经测试表明，代理人能维持盈利的同时确保任务执行效率。该方法对高频交易等去中心化市场算法策略具备潜在应用价值。

title: Mosaic: Multi-Session Agentic Reinforcement Learning
summary: Most existing agentic reinforcement learning methods assume single-session trajectories, where interaction proceeds within one continuously accumulated context. However, agentic techniques such as context compaction and subagent forking may produce trajectories spanning multiple sessions, creating a mismatch between the single-session training assumption and inference-time execution. Therefore, we introduce Multi-Session Agentic Reinforcement Learning, a more general setting that supports an arbitrary number of sessions within a trajectory. Under this setting, a widely adopted method is to broadcast trajectory-level advantages to all sessions, but this does not distinguish contributions from various sessions or guide session allocation within trajectories. To address this issue, we propose Mosaic, a multi-session agentic RL method with critic-free hierarchical optimization. At the trajectory level, it incorporates session-usage signals into advantage estimation. At the session level, it shapes each session's advantage according to the estimated marginal contribution. Experiments on BrowseComp with Qwen3.5-4B show that Mosaic outperforms broadcasting in both context compaction and subagent forking scenarios while using fewer sessions on average. Further analyses show that our method achieves improvements in session utility and allocation, which we suggested is a promising target for future advances in multi-session agentic RL.
core_methodology: Mosaic introduces a multi-session agentic reinforcement learning method with critic-free hierarchical optimization. It incorporates session-usage signals into advantage estimation at the trajectory level and shapes each session's advantage according to the estimated marginal contribution at the session level.
data_sources: Experiments conducted on BrowseComp with Qwen3.5-4B, suggesting the potential for adaptation to financial market data.
alpha_potential: The method's ability to optimize and allocate sessions effectively within trajectories could be adapted for dynamic portfolio allocation or trading strategy optimization, albeit requiring significant domain-specific adaptation.
title_cn: Mosaic：多会话智能体强化学习

title: Progress Reward Model for Reinforcement Learning via Large Language Models
summary: Traditional reinforcement learning (RL) algorithms face significant limitations in handling long-term tasks with sparse rewards. Recent advancements have leveraged large language models (LLMs) to enhance RL by utilizing their world knowledge for task planning and reward generation. However, planning-based approaches often depend on pre-defined skill libraries and fail to optimize low-level control policies, while reward-based methods require extensive human feedback or exhaustive searching due to the complexity of tasks. In this paper, we propose the Progress Reward Model for RL (PRM4RL), a novel framework that integrates task planning and dense reward to enhance RL. For high-level planning, a complex task is decomposed into a series of simple manageable subtasks, with a subtask-oriented, fine-grained progress function designed to monitor task execution progress. For low-level reward generation, inspired by potential-based reward shaping, we use the progress function to construct a Progress Reward Model (PRM), providing theoretically grounded optimality and convergence guarantees, thereby enabling effective policy optimization. Experimental results on robotics control tasks demonstrate that our approach outperforms both LLM-based planning and reward methods, achieving state-of-the-art performance. Code is available at https://github.com/deng-ai-lab/PRM4RL.
core_methodology: A novel framework called PRM4RL that integrates task planning and dense reward generation in reinforcement learning. It decomposes complex tasks into simpler subtasks with a progress function for monitoring execution and uses this function to construct a Progress Reward Model (PRM) for policy optimization.
data_sources: Robotics control tasks (not financial data directly, but methodology could be adapted to financial tasks)
alpha_potential: Potential for optimizing trading strategies by decomposing complex portfolio management problems into simpler subtasks and using progress-based reward shaping for better policy optimization. Could be adapted for execution algorithms or dynamic portfolio management.
title_cn: 基于大型语言模型的强化学习进展奖励模型
summary_cn: 本研究提出的PRM4RL框架结合任务规划和密集奖励生成，通过将复杂任务分解为简单子任务并设计进度函数优化策略。该方法虽然在机器人控制任务中验证，但其基于进度的奖励模型可潜在应用于量化交易策略优化，如组合管理或执行算法的分阶段优化。

title: Rethinking Successive Rejects Algorithms
summary: In the best-arm identification problem, an algorithm adaptively selects arms to find the arm of the largest mean reward. Successive Rejects (SR) is a simple fixed-budget best-arm identification algorithm that eliminates one candidate arm at each phase. At first glance, SR seems to have limited adaptivity, since it follows predetermined phase lengths. However, for Gaussian arms with common variance, SR's worst-instance error exponent normalized by the popular complexity measure $H_1(P)$ is optimal up to a constant factor, which partly explains why SR's performance is competitive compared with state-of-the-art adaptive sampling algorithms. In this paper, we extend the framework of SR by optimizing its predefined schedule of phase lengths. We formulate phase-schedule design as an optimization problem for the normalized error exponent. Then, we introduce a version of SR with the optimized schedule, which we call $H_1$-balanced Successive Rejects ($H_1$-SR). This schedule is optimal within the class of SR-type algorithms with deterministic equal-count schedules. For Gaussian arms with common variance, $H_1$-SR achieves at least $11/12$ of the optimal normalized rate over all adaptive algorithms for every $K\ge2$, and this approximation ratio converges to one as $1-O(1/\log K)$ as $K\to\infty$. This is a significant improvement over original SR, whose corresponding fraction of the optimal normalized rate converges to $1/4$. Finally, experiments on ten synthetic instances and two dataset-derived Gaussian benchmarks compare the optimized schedule with original SR at finite horizons. They show substantial gains on many instances while also exposing a regime in which more aggressive early elimination is costly.
core_methodology: The paper introduces an optimized version of the Successive Rejects (SR) algorithm, called H1-balanced Successive Rejects (H1-SR), for best-arm identification in bandit problems. The methodology focuses on optimizing the phase lengths of the SR algorithm to improve the error exponent, particularly for Gaussian arms with common variance.
data_sources: The paper uses synthetic instances and dataset-derived Gaussian benchmarks for experimental validation.
alpha_potential: The optimized SR algorithm could potentially be applied to portfolio optimization and asset selection problems in quantitative finance, where identifying the best-performing assets (arms) with limited samples (budget) is crucial.
title_cn: 重新思考连续拒绝算法
